claims.claim: **Most urticaria is idiopathic or viral**; viral infection is a common cause in children, during or after the illness.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urticaria' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urticaria/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Urticaria with airway, respiratory, cardiovascular or gastrointestinal involvement: suspect anaphylaxis — urgent adrenaline and medical assessment.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urticaria' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urticaria/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Acute: under 6 weeks. Chronic: most days for more than 6 weeks** — usually idiopathic, sometimes inducible or autoimmune.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urticaria' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urticaria/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Suspect allergy when episodes are rare, short-lived and circumstantial**: only with exercise, every time in the 1–2 hours after a meal, or with abdominal pain, vomiting, breathing difficulty or dizziness.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urticaria' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urticaria/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Allergic urticaria appears within 1–2 hours of exposure and fades within 6–8 hours. Urticaria lasting days is almost never allergy** (except some medication allergies).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urticaria' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urticaria/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Urticaria during an antibiotic course is often the infection, not antibiotic allergy.** Take a detailed drug allergy history; consider drug allergy clinic referral.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urticaria' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urticaria/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Wheals are well circumscribed, often coalescent, usually gone within 24 hours, and migrate** from site to site within minutes to hours.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urticaria' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urticaria/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Angioedema** is larger, painful rather than itchy, and may take up to 72 hours to resolve.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urticaria' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urticaria/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Urticaria: non-target lesions with central pallor. Erythema multiforme: target lesions with central purpura.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urticaria' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urticaria/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Urticarial vasculitis (including HSP):** painful, lasts over 48 hours, leaves discolouration.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urticaria' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urticaria/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Recurrent angioedema without wheals: think C1 esterase inhibitor deficiency** — urticaria is not a feature of it.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urticaria' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urticaria/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Acute urticaria almost never needs investigation, and routine allergy testing is unnecessary** (a common misconception worth discussing). They may be indicated in chronic urticaria with features of an underlying cause.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urticaria' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urticaria/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Most acute cases resolve untreated in days to weeks.** Remove triggers, avoid heat and spicy food, **avoid NSAIDs**, use a cool compress.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urticaria' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urticaria/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Non-sedating antihistamine, e.g. cetirizine orally:** 6–11 months 0.25 mg/kg daily (max 2.5 mg) · 1–2 years 2.5 mg twice daily · 2–6 years 5 mg daily or 2.5 mg twice daily · 6–12 years 10 mg daily or 5 mg twice daily · 12–18 years 10 mg daily.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urticaria' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urticaria/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Severe and not responding to antihistamines:** consider one oral dose of 0.5–1 mg/kg of prednisolone (max 60 mg). **Steroid creams are not effective.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urticaria' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urticaria/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Chronic urticaria:** start as for acute; if ongoing, **cetirizine may be increased to as much as 4 times its recommended daily dose** (6 years and older: max 40 mg total daily), and a sedating antihistamine may be added. Still persisting: specialist advice; immunomodulators only with an allergy specialist.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urticaria' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urticaria/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discuss with the paediatric team:** fever, bruising, joint pain or systemic features · anaphylaxis · angioedema · age under 6 months · chronic urticaria over 6 weeks.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urticaria' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urticaria/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge once anaphylaxis is excluded — most children do not need admission.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urticaria' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urticaria/, retrieved 2026-09-23
